# A timeline bar is announced with day keys and one day too many

Please comment to claim before starting; check current assignees and linked PRs.

## Context

Every bar in `Neo.timeline.Column` (the scheduler, the Gantt chart and the timeline examples render through it) is a button with an `aria-label`, so a screen reader announces that label for the bar. The label names the bar's dates as storage keys, and a bar that ends at midnight is announced with one day more than it covers. The header above the same bars already formats its dates for the reader's language.

## The Problem

- `examples/gantt/basic/` (axis zone `UTC`): "Survey the site" runs from `2026-11-09T00:00:00Z` to `2026-11-10T00:00:00Z` and is drawn as one day. Its accessible name is `Survey the site (2026-11-09 – 2026-11-10)`: two days, written `YYYY-MM-DD`.
- `examples/scheduler/basic/` (axis zone `UTC`): the booking "Live tracking" runs from 08:00 to 13:00 on 2026-11-10 and is announced as `Live tracking (2026-11-10 – 2026-11-10)`: the date twice and no times.
- A Gantt milestone has no length (`endDate` equal to `startDate`, as in `test/playwright/unit/gantt/DependencyCreation.spec.mjs:55`) and is announced as `Inspection (2026-11-16 – 2026-11-16)`.

Reproduced on `dev` at `09061d53ac` through `Column#cellRenderer`, with the machine zone set to `America/Los_Angeles` and to `Pacific/Auckland`: all three labels come out as above in both zones.

## The Architectural Reality

- `src/timeline/Column.mjs:668–670` builds the label from `(me.timeAxis || TimeAxis).dayKey(startDate)` and `.dayKey(endDate)`. `TimeAxis#dayKey` (`src/timeline/TimeAxis.mjs:650`) returns a `YYYY-MM-DD` key in the axis zone: an identifier, not display text.
- A bar's `endDate` is exclusive: its right edge is `timeAxis.dateToOffset(clampedEndMs)` (`src/timeline/Column.mjs:976`).
- `Neo.gantt.Column#buildBarVdom` (`src/gantt/Column.mjs:17`) calls the timeline column's `buildBarVdom`, so Gantt bars and milestones get the same label.
- The header already formats dates for people, and `Column.mjs` already imports it:
  - `TimeAxisHeader.formatWall(locale, options, wall, wallEnd)` (`src/timeline/TimeAxisHeader.mjs:35`) wraps `Intl.DateTimeFormat`, and formats a range with `formatRange` when `wallEnd` is given.
  - `TimeAxisHeader.lastWallMoment(axis, tick)` (`TimeAxisHeader.mjs:53`) turns an exclusive `endDate` into the last moment inside the range.
  - `axis.wallTime(date)` moves a date into the axis zone.
  - The header's language is `locale_`, default `Neo.config.locale` (`TimeAxisHeader.mjs:109–113`). `Column` has no locale config.
- Design authority: `TimeAxisHeader#formatMajorTick` — "Formats a major tick label using `majorFormatter`, or a `locale` label in the axis' zone"; `TimeAxisHeader.lastWallMoment` — "Returns the last wall-clock moment of a tick, whose `endDate` is exclusive." The bar's label is the same family's date text.

## The Fix

In `src/timeline/Column.mjs`:

1. Add a reactive `locale_` config, default `Neo.config.locale`, documented like the header's.
2. Build the label's dates with `TimeAxisHeader.formatWall(me.locale, options, wall, wallEnd)`, where `wall = axis.wallTime(startDate)`:
   - a bar that starts and ends at midnight in the axis zone names days only (`{month: 'short', day: 'numeric'}`), with `wallEnd = TimeAxisHeader.lastWallMoment(axis, {endDate})`, so a one-day bar names one day;
   - any other bar adds hours and minutes, with `wallEnd = axis.wallTime(endDate)`: `lastWallMoment` here would announce a booking that ends at 13:00 as ending at 12:59;
   - a bar without length (`endDate <= startDate`) passes no `wallEnd` and names one moment. With `lastWallMoment`, a milestone at midnight would read as the reversed range `Nov 16 – 15`: V8's `formatRange` returns it without an error.
3. Keep the title first, and keep the `barKey` fallback for a bar without a title.

A probe of exactly this rule on `dev`, through the real `formatWall`, `lastWallMoment` and `wallTime`, printed `Survey the site (Nov 9)`, `Nov 12 – 13` for a two-day bar, `Live tracking (Nov 10, 08:00 – 13:00)`, `Inspection (Nov 16)` and `Handover (Nov 17, 14:00)` in `en-US`, and `9. Nov.` for the one-day bar in `de-DE`, the same in both machine zones above.

Add unit tests to `test/playwright/unit/timeline/Column.spec.mjs`. Set `locale` and the axis `timeZone` explicitly in each test, because `Neo.config.locale` defaults to the machine's language. `formatRange` puts thin spaces (U+2009) around its dash in `en-US`, so build each expected string with `Intl.DateTimeFormat` in the test instead of typing it.

| Target Surface | Source of Authority | Proposed Behavior | Fallback | Docs | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Neo.timeline.Column#locale_` (new) | `TimeAxisHeader#locale_` (same family) | the language of each bar's accessible name | `Neo.config.locale` | JSDoc on the config | the new unit tests |
| a bar's `aria-label` | `TimeAxisHeader#formatMajorTick`, `lastWallMoment` | `<title> (<dates in the locale, exclusive end>)` | `barKey` when the bar has no title | none | the new unit tests |

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1: With `locale: 'en-US'` on a `UTC` axis, a bar from `2026-11-09T00:00Z` to `2026-11-10T00:00Z` titled "Survey the site" is announced as `Survey the site (Nov 9)`, and a two-day bar names two days (for example `Nov 12 – 13`).
- [ ] AC-2: A bar from 08:00 to 13:00 on one day names that date once and reads from 08:00 to 13:00 (for example `Nov 10, 08:00 – 13:00` with `hourCycle: 'h23'`), never 12:59.
- [ ] AC-3: A bar without length names its one date (`Nov 16` at midnight) or its date and time (`Nov 17, 14:00`), never a range.
- [ ] AC-4: With `locale: 'de-DE'`, the one-day bar is announced as `Survey the site (9. Nov.)`.
- [ ] AC-5: The text is computed in the axis zone: with `timeZone: 'UTC'` on the axis, the label does not depend on the machine's time zone.
- [ ] AC-6: `npx playwright test -c test/playwright/playwright.config.unit.mjs test/playwright/unit/timeline/Column.spec.mjs` passes, including the new tests.

## Out of Scope

- Passing one locale from the scheduler or Gantt container to both the header and the column.
- The bar's visible label and `barRenderer` overrides.
- The header's formatting, and the calendar, which keeps its own time scale.
